cards.text: Friend, this one's heavy, so pull up a stool. Babylon's army has burned Jerusalem and broken down her walls (Jeremiah 52:13-14). Now the writer of Lamentations looks at the city and cries, "How lonely lies the city, once so full of people!"

cards.question: Everything has flipped for Jerusalem. She was great among the nations, and now she's a widow. And the princess of the provinces? She has become a ___.

cards.text: In the night, she weeps aloud with tears upon her cheeks. She's got lovers and friends, so let's see who shows up.

cards.question: The writer says all of Jerusalem's friends have betrayed her. What have those friends become?
Out of all her lovers, at least one comes to comfort Jerusalem.

cards.text: Judah, Jerusalem's kingdom, has gone into exile, under affliction and harsh slavery. All her pursuers have caught up with her in the middle of her distress.

cards.question: Judah is in exile now, living among the nations. What does she find there?

cards.text: Even the roads to Zion, the City of David (2 Samuel 5:7), mourn, because no one comes to her appointed feasts. Her gates are deserted, her priests groan and her maidens grieve.

cards.question: Jerusalem's foes have become her masters. The writer says the LORD has brought her this grief. Because of what?

cards.text: Her children have gone away as captives before the enemy. All the splendor has departed from the Daughter of Zion.

cards.question: The writer says Jerusalem's princes are like deer that find no pasture. What happens when the hunter comes?

cards.text: In her wandering, Jerusalem remembers all the treasures that were hers in days of old. I did that for years in the junk drawer, friend, telling the dust all about my glory days, and the dust was NOT impressed.

cards.question: When Jerusalem's people fell into enemy hands, no help came. The writer says her enemies looked away in shame.

cards.text: The writer doesn't soften it: Jerusalem has sinned greatly. Everyone who honored her now despises her, and she groans and turns away.

cards.question: Her uncleanness stains her skirts. The writer says Jerusalem saw her downfall coming a long way off.
There's no one to comfort her. Then Jerusalem herself cries out for the first time. Who does she ask to look on her affliction?

cards.text: The adversary seizes all her treasures. And she has seen the nations walk into her sanctuary.

cards.question: The nations entered Jerusalem's sanctuary. They were the very ones God had ___ to enter His assembly.

cards.text: All her people groan as they search for bread. Then Jerusalem cries out again: "Look, O LORD, and consider, for I have become despised."

cards.question: To keep themselves alive, Jerusalem's people trade their treasures for food.

cards.text: Up to now the writer's been doing most of the talking. Now Jerusalem takes over and calls out to everyone on the road: "Is this nothing to you, all you who pass by?"

cards.question: Jerusalem tells everyone passing by to look around and see. What does she want to know?

answers.text: If any sorrow is like hers

cards.question: Jerusalem says the LORD made her suffer on the day of His fierce anger.

cards.text: She doesn't just say it hurts, friend. She paints it: the LORD sent fire from on high that overpowered her bones, and He spread a net for her feet.

cards.question: The net the Lord spreads for Jerusalem's feet carries her safely home.

cards.text: Then her transgressions get a picture of their own: they're bound into a yoke, knit together by His hand.

cards.question: Jerusalem says her transgressions are bound into a yoke and draped over her ___.

cards.text: Friend, this is where I'd put the dough down for a minute. The Lord has broken her strength and handed her over to those she cannot withstand.

cards.question: Jerusalem says the Lord has trampled the Virgin Daughter of Judah like grapes in a winepress. She says He has honored all the mighty men in her midst.

cards.text: She weeps, and her children are destitute because the enemy has prevailed. Then the writer steps back in, and friend, Zion stretches out her hands with no one to comfort her.

cards.question: The writer speaks of Jacob here, meaning the people who came from Jacob, Isaac's son (Genesis 25:26). What does he say the LORD has decreed against Jacob?
Jerusalem speaks again. She says the LORD is ___, yet she rebelled against His command.

cards.text: Now she's calling out to everyone in earshot: listen, and look upon her suffering.

cards.question: Jerusalem tells all the people to look upon her suffering. Who does she say has gone into captivity?

cards.text: She called out to her lovers, but they betrayed her. Her priests and elders died in the city while they searched for food to keep themselves alive.

cards.question: Then Jerusalem turns back to the LORD. What does she ask Him to see?

answers.text: How strong her walls still are

cards.text: She says she's churning within, because she has been most rebellious. Outside, the sword bereaves, and inside, there is death.

cards.question: People hear Jerusalem groaning, but no one comforts her. Her enemies hear about her trouble too, and they are glad that the LORD caused it.
Jerusalem asks the LORD to bring the day He has announced and to deal with her enemies. How does she ask Him to deal with them?

answers.text: As He has dealt with her

cards.text: And the poem ends right where her heart is: "For my groans are many, and my heart is faint."
